title: A Clean Slate for Offline Reinforcement Learning

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Claims 'average training speedups of 131.5x and 74.8x against OfflineRL-Kit [16] and CORL [17]'. The paper's own Table 2 (Appendix F) yields computed speedups of only ~6.1-20.8x vs OfflineRL-Kit (mean ~14.5x) and ~1.3-18.4x vs CORL (mean ~11x), and Figure 5 caps per-algorithm speedups at 16x. The headline numbers are off by roughly an order of magnitude relative to the paper's own data.

States 'The unification concept traces back to online RL architectures like Rainbow [38] and Muesli [39]' and 'Other dual optimization frameworks [40]...'. In the paper's own reference list, [38] is Stable-Baselines3 (Raffin et al.), [39] is Spinning Up (Achiam), and [40] is rejax (Liesen et al.). The correct references are [25] (Hessel et al., Rainbow), [26] (Hessel et al., Muesli), and [27] (Sikchi et al., Dual RL), which Appendix L.3 cites correctly for the identical claims.

Direct self-contradiction within one paragraph: 'MoBRAC outperforms other model-based methods for all datasets, except for MOPO in maze2d-large-v1' (8 wins / 1 non-win of 9) versus 'MoBRAC outperforms the other model-based methods in 6 out of 9 datasets and is tied with MOPO for 3 others (Appendix K)' (6 wins / 3 ties). Both accounts cover all 9 datasets and are mutually exclusive.

States experiments are run 'without equalizing the online tuning budgets or computational cost across methods' and that uncontrolled tuning budgets are a practice 'which we continue here for consistency with original papers'. This contradicts the paper's central methodological contribution (Abstract: 'transparent evaluation procedure that explicitly quantifies online tuning budgets'; Section 3.2: fixed budget of N pre-deployment interactions applied uniformly, Figure 3 evaluating all methods at identical bandit-pull budgets). As written, the Results section describes doing exactly what the proposed procedure exists to eliminate.

Caption reads 'Full comparison of TD3-AWR to prior model-based methods across all datasets', but the figure's legend and panels compare TD3-AWR against IQL and ReBRAC, both model-free algorithms; TD3-AWR itself is introduced in Section 5.1 as the paper's model-free method. The model-based comparison is Figure 15 (MoBRAC).

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3.3 (Distractor Policy Phenomenon) vs Section 3.2 and Appendix D
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Section 3.3 asserts performance dips 'are common artifacts of statistical fluctuations and sampling noise' and 'likely reflect noise rather than fundamental flaws', while Section 3.2 says 'The importance of this is demonstrated by the emergence of distractor policies' and Appendix D systematically shows 'the probability of preferring an unstable policy increases over time' (mean over 100K random policy orderings) with dips growing as more policies are subsampled. The paper simultaneously dismisses and demonstrates the same systematic effect.

The augmented value target is printed as v_hat_{t+1} = v_{t+1} + alpha_BC * (a_tilde_{t+1} - a_{t+1}) + alpha_H * H(pi). The BC term is a raw difference of action vectors added to a scalar (not a scalar for multi-dimensional actions, missing the squared norm), and its sign is positive whereas a behaviour-cloning penalty must reduce the target for actions deviating from the dataset action (ReBRAC-style: v - alpha_BC * ||a_tilde - a||^2). As printed, the unified critic target does not reduce to the ReBRAC/TD3-BC objectives it claims to encapsulate.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 4.2 (Actor Objective) vs Appendix I.2 Eq. (8) and Table 5
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Section 4.2 defines L_actor with five terms (beta_q, beta_BC, beta_H, beta_div, beta_dyn), but Appendix I.2 Eq. (8) defines the same unified actor loss with only three terms (no beta_div or beta_dyn), and Eq. (7) places the diversity term in the critic loss (as in EDAC), not the actor loss. Additionally, Section 4.2 claims the critic objective includes 'all referenced methods, including CQL despite its complexity', yet Table 5 (Unifloral hyperparameters of prior algorithms) contains no CQL column.

States TD3-AWR 'underperforms or matches [ReBRAC] on others, such as pen-human and kitchen-mixed', but the paper's own Figure 6 reports pen-human-v1: TD3-AWR ~65-70 vs ReBRAC ~40, and Appendix J reports kitchen-mixed-v0: TD3-AWR ~35 vs ReBRAC ~30 - TD3-AWR outperforms ReBRAC on both named examples (it trails IQL on kitchen-mixed, not ReBRAC).

Self-contradictory recommendation: warns that 'limiting evaluation to [MuJoCo locomotion and Adroit tasks from the D4RL suite] risks overfitting hyperparameters to these domains', then immediately recommends 'focusing on widely used tasks such as hopper-medium-v2, halfcheetah-medium-expert-v2, ..., pen-human-v1, ... from the canonical D4RL dataset' - i.e., exactly the D4RL tasks it just cautioned against limiting evaluation to.

predicted_errors.error_location: Figure 11b (Appendix E) vs Appendix E.2 and Figure 10c
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Figure 11b reports Unifloral's line-differences from CQL as LARGER than baselines' (BC: Unifloral 672 vs CORL 544 vs JAX-CORL 201; EDAC: 945 vs 674 vs 230; ReBRAC: 945 vs 658 vs 208), contradicting E.2's claim 'We minimize the number of lines between implementations' and Figure 10c where Unifloral parent-child diffs are dramatically smaller than CORL's (CQL<-SAC-N: 38 vs 944; EDAC<-SAC-N: 23 vs 63). Either the columns are inverted or the minimal-difference claim is falsified by the paper's own data.

predicted_errors.error_location: Table 2 (Appendix F), ReBRAC row vs Figure 5
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Table 2 gives ReBRAC training time as 8.7 min (CORL) vs 6.8 min (Unifloral), a speedup of ~1.28x, directly contradicting Figure 5's claimed 8x ReBRAC speedup. The 8.7 value is also an extreme outlier against all other CORL times (15.0-180.3 min); ~54-87 min would be consistent with the claimed 8x. One of the two reported values must be wrong.

summary: Exhaustive strict-mode verification of 'A Clean Slate for Offline Reinforcement Learning' (80 snippets, all verified) found 12 above-threshold errors, 6 of them high-confidence (>=0.85). The most serious: (1) headline training-speedup claims of 131.5x/74.8x in the Introduction are contradicted by the paper's own Table 2 and Figure 5, which support only ~6-21x; (2) Related Work cites Rainbow, Muesli, and dual-optimization frameworks as [38]-[40], which in the paper's own bibliography are Stable-Baselines3, Spinning Up, and rejax (correct entries are [25]-[27], used correctly in Appendix L); (3) Section 5.2 contradicts itself within one paragraph on MoBRAC's win count (all-but-one vs 6-of-9-plus-3-ties); (4) Section 3.3 states tuning budgets were NOT equalized or controlled, directly contradicting the paper's central contribution of a fixed, transparent tuning-budget evaluation procedure; (5) Figure 14's caption calls IQL/ReBRAC 'model-based methods' when they and TD3-AWR are model-free; (6) Section 3.3 dismisses distractor-policy dips as sampling noise while Section 3.2 and Appendix D systematically demonstrate the phenomenon. Additional confirmed issues include an ill-formed BC term in the unified critic target (Eq. 5: un-squared, wrong-signed action difference), a 5-term vs 3-term contradiction between the main-text and appendix definitions of the unified actor objective (plus a claimed-but-absent CQL column in Table 5), a self-contradictory dataset recommendation in Section 3.2, TD3-AWR/ReBRAC comparisons in Section 5.1 that invert the paper's own figure values, an inverted code-diff table (Figure 11b) contradicting the minimal-diff claim, and a ReBRAC training-time entry in Table 2 (8.7 min) inconsistent with the claimed 8x speedup. Noted below threshold (not counted as errors): Table 3's anomalously low CQL scores versus the 'matching prior implementations' claim (externally unverifiable here), the Conclusion's 'superior performance over a wide range of tasks' overclaim versus Section 5.1's hedged results, and a walker2d panel description exceeding its stated y-axis range. Verdict: NEEDS_CORRECTION.
